text:
maya-support: FYI customer reports calls to internal service endpoint are suddenly hitting the public ELB and failing TLS checks. They say it started after a config push earlier this morning. attaching initial repro info.

acme-customer: timeline: 2026-03-17 09:12 UTC. VPC vpc-0a1b2c3d, account 9876543210. From a pod in us-west-2 we get the public IP for svc.internal.acme instead of the private svc endpoint IP. curl fails with certificate CN mismatch.

acme-customer: dig output from pod:```
$ kubectl exec -it pod/web-5 -- dig +short svc.internal.acme
34.201.12.45
```

acme-customer: dig from bastion in same VPC:```
$ dig +short svc.internal.acme @10.0.0.2
10.0.4.89
```

maya-support: that looks like split-horizon answers depending on resolver path. can you paste /etc/resolv.conf from the pod and from the node? also curl -v output (showing cert CN) would help.

acme-customer: pod /etc/resolv.conf:```
search default.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local
nameserver 169.254.20.10
options ndots:5
```
node /etc/resolv.conf:```
nameserver 10.0.0.2
```

curl -v from pod:```
* Connected to svc.internal.acme (34.201.12.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake completed with CN: "*.external.acme.com"
* SSL: certificate subject name '*.external.acme.com' does not match 'svc.internal.acme'
```

chen-eng-sre: thanks. node-local resolver (169.254.20.10) is returning public answer. that suggests the node-local cache/forwarder is using a forwarder path that reaches public Route53 resolver or an external forwarder which sees the public hosted zone. can you run `dig +noall +answer svc.internal.acme @169.254.20.10` from inside the pod and paste?

acme-customer: dig @169.254.20.10:```
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; ANSWER SECTION:
svc.internal.acme. 60 IN A 34.201.12.45
```

chen-eng-sre: interesting — node-local forwarder giving public answer. two likely causes: 1) private hosted zone was accidentally detached from VPC (Route53 will then return public zone records), or 2) a resolver rule/forwarder change causes queries to go to an upstream that resolves public zone.

oliver-platform: @chen-eng-sre I ran a quick audit against Route53 change logs for account 9876543210 and saw a VPC association removal event for hosted zone ZABCDEFGHI around 4112340000 by an automation role. dns-bot should have a record.

_dns-bot_: Route53 change detected: private hosted zone ZABCDEFGHI disassociated from VPC vpc-0a1b2c3d at 2026-03-17T08:40:05Z (change-id /change/Z0XYZ). Actor: infra-automation-role.

maya-support: that lines up with the customer's timeline. probably the disassociation caused the node-local resolver to get a public answer. if we re-associate the hosted zone with the VPC, the private answer should return. steps: 1) re-associate hosted zone ZABCDEFGHI -> vpc-0a1b2c3d (via console or aws cli), 2) restart node-local-dns/sidecar or flush cache on nodes (kubectl rollout restart ds/node-local-dns -n kube-system), 3) check dig @169.254.20.10 again.

chen-eng-sre: added: also check any VPC resolver rule overrides in the account that might forward queries to a cross-account resolver which would see the public zone. run `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rule-associations --filters Key=VPCId,Values=vpc-0a1b2c3d` and confirm.

acme-customer: re-association in progress by our infra team now. will restart node-local cache after association.

maya-support: temporary mitigation for app while infra fixes: in your deployment you can add an init container to write the internal IP to /etc/hosts or use curl --resolve to force internal IP for health checks, but that's a brittle workaround. prefer fixing hosted zone association.

acme-customer: re-association completed. after restarting node-local-ds pods dig @169.254.20.10 now returns:```
svc.internal.acme. 60 IN A 10.0.4.89
```

acme-customer: curl -v now connects to 10.0.4.89 and TLS CN matches svc.internal.acme, requests succeed.

maya-support: great — marking as resolved. follow-ups: 1) we recommend adding an automation guard to prevent accidental disassociation (IAM condition on automation role), 2) add a quick synthetic check that queries internal endpoints from a pod after infra runs.

chen-eng-sre: added a ticket to infra backlog to add the IAM guard and synthetic check. thanks everyone. :party:
summary: Customer reported internal service endpoint resolving to public IP from pods due to private hosted zone disassociation; triaged by support and eng, re-associated hosted zone, restarted node-local dns, verified fix; recommended IAM guard and synthetic checks.
